note: Variants clustered in the 5' coding region of TRA2B cause Ramond-Elliott syndrome, with infantile spasms and early-onset epilepsy reported in over half of affected individuals.

evidence.text: Variants clustered in the 5' part of TRA2B lead to developmental delay and intellectual disability, frequently accompanied by infantile spasms and microcephaly.

source.title: Clustered variants in the 5′ coding region of TRA2B cause a distinctive neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: All variants clustered in the 5' part of TRA2B, upstream of an alternative translation start site responsible for the expression of the noncanonical Tra2β-3 isoform. All affected individuals presented intellectual disability and/or developmental delay, frequently associated with infantile spasms, microcephaly, brain anomalies, autism spectrum disorder, feeding difficulties, and short stature.

evidence.text: About 58% of affected individuals experienced early-onset seizures between 3 and 9 months of age, predominantly manifesting as infantile spasms.

source.title: 621421 - RAMOND-ELLIOTT NEURODEVELOPMENTAL SYNDROME; RAMELN
source.quote: About half (58%) had early-onset seizures between 3 and 9 months of age, mostly infantile spasms.
